sentences.text: Purpose.
sentences.say: Purpose.

sentences.text: A computer cannot look at a plot and say "that line looks good".
sentences.say: A computer cannot look at a plot and say "that line looks good".

sentences.text: It needs one number that measures how wrong a line is, and the training task becomes making that number small.
sentences.say: It needs one number that measures how wrong a line is, and the training task becomes making that number small.

sentences.text: Key ideas
sentences.say: Key ideas

sentences.text: The cost J(w, b) is the average squared error, with a factor 1/2 that tidies later maths.
sentences.say: The cost J(w, b) is the average squared error, with a factor 1/2 that tidies later maths.

sentences.text: A lower cost means a better fit, so training means minimizing J.
sentences.say: A lower cost means a better fit, so training means minimizing J.

sentences.text: J as a function of w and b is a bowl.
sentences.say: J as a function of w and b is a bowl.

sentences.text: The bottom of the bowl is the best line.
sentences.say: The bottom of the bowl is the best line.

sentences.text: Squared error for linear regression gives a bowl with a single bottom (convex), so there are no traps.
sentences.say: Squared error for linear regression gives a bowl with a single bottom (convex), so there are no traps.

sentences.text: 5.1 The formula
sentences.say: 5.1 The formula

sentences.text: Read it from the inside out: the error of example i, squared, added over all m examples, divided by m to get an average (so that the number does not grow just because you have more data), and divided by 2 as well.
sentences.say: Read it from the inside out: the error of example i, squared, added over all m examples, divided by m to get an average (so that the number does not grow just because you have more data), and divided by 2 as well.

sentences.text: The extra 2 does nothing to the answer: it only cancels the 2 that appears when you take the derivative in Chapter 6.
sentences.say: The extra 2 does nothing to the answer: it only cancels the 2 that appears when you take the derivative in Chapter 6.

sentences.say: 5.2 A worked example

sentences.text: Use the three points (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3) and fix b = 0, so the cost depends only on w. For w = 0.5:

J equals 1 divided by (2 times 3) times ( (0.5 minus 1) squared plus (1 minus 2) squared plus (1.5 minus 3) squared ) equals (0.25 plus 1 plus 2.25) divided by 6 equals 0.583

sentences.text: Plot cost against w and you get a parabola (a U shape) whose lowest point is at w = 1.
sentences.say: Plot cost against w and you get a parabola (a U shape) whose lowest point is at w equals 1.

sentences.text: The goal of linear regression is to find the w and b that sit at the bottom.

sentences.text: 5.3 Seeing the bowl
sentences.say: 5.3 Seeing the bowl

sentences.text: With both w and b free, J is a surface over a plane: a bowl, like a soup bowl or a hammock.
sentences.say: With both w and b free, J is a surface over a plane: a bowl, like a soup bowl or a hammock.

sentences.text: A contour plot shows the same bowl from above, like a topographic map: every ring is a set of (w, b) pairs with the same cost, and the centre is the minimum.
sentences.say: A contour plot shows the same bowl from above, like a topographic map: every ring is a set of (w, b) pairs with the same cost, and the centre is the minimum.

sentences.text: In Ng's housing example a point far from the centre (w about -0.15, b about 800) is a very bad line, while points near the centre fit well.
sentences.say: In Ng's housing example a point far from the centre (w about -0.15, b about 800) is a very bad line, while points near the centre fit well.

sentences.text: Reading such plots by hand does not scale, so we need an algorithm that walks to the centre by itself.
sentences.say: Reading such plots by hand does not scale, so we need an algorithm that walks to the centre by itself.

sentences.text: That is gradient descent.
sentences.say: That is gradient descent.

sentences.text: 5.4 Convex: one bottom, no traps
sentences.say: 5.4 Convex: one bottom, no traps

sentences.text: The squared-error cost of linear regression is convex: one bowl, one lowest point, no side valleys.
sentences.say: The squared-error cost of linear regression is convex: one bowl, one lowest point, no side valleys.

sentences.text: Wherever you start, going downhill ends at the global minimum.
sentences.say: Wherever you start, going downhill ends at the global minimum.

sentences.text: The cost surface of a neural network is not convex.
sentences.say: The cost surface of a neural network is not convex.

sentences.text: It has many valleys (local minima), and where training ends depends on where it started.
sentences.say: It has many valleys (local minima), and where training ends depends on where it started.

sentences.text: Common mistakes
sentences.say: Common mistakes

sentences.text: Comparing the cost of two models on different datasets, or one on training and one on test data.
sentences.say: Comparing the cost of two models on different datasets, or one on training and one on test data.
